title: dome-mirror's sync-workspace-step4c.js doesn't propagate deletions — FUSE accumulates whatever prune deletes from git
context:
2026-06-10 morning audit revealed a divergence between origin/main and FUSE workspace for the monitor/integrity/ per-run artifact categories. Background: prune-integrity ran cleanly today (2026-06-10T08:06Z) with no cap pressure (capped=0 across all policies). It archived 1,680 files in one run: 802 workspace-sync-runs, 498 verify-pending-run, 305 narrative-cite-audit, 75 push-failure. GitHub Contents API confirms origin/main no longer has those files (5/5 spot-checks returned HTTP 404). So the git side is clean.

But the FUSE workspace still has them. Counts measured at the time of audit:
  - workspace-sync-runs/: 955 live (794 older than 7-day retention, eligible for archive on git side already done)
  - verify-pending-run-*.json: 795 live (490 over 14-day retention)
  - narrative-cite-audit-*.json: 316 live (~305 over retention; estimated 430 MB of FUSE-side orphans since prune reclaimed 427 MB on git side)

Root cause located in monitor/scripts/sync-workspace-step4c.js: the script has ZERO `unlink` / `delete` / `rmSync` / `fs.rm` calls. It only propagates copies (smart_copy git→FUSE). When origin removes a file, the script does not propagate the removal. So FUSE accumulates whatever prune deletes from git, indefinitely.

This is NOT the same bug as PROP-082 (prune↔workspace-sync re-add loop). PROP-082 prevented FUSE→git universal-pusher from re-adding stale files to origin (and the spot-check confirms it's working — orphans aren't getting re-pushed to git). The remaining gap is the OTHER direction: git→FUSE doesn't catch deletions.
task: Investigate and propose a safe fix for dome-mirror's delete-propagation gap.
constraints: Disaster sensitivity: the 2026-05-21 workspace-sync mass-delete event taught us that LLM agents under disk pressure improvise unsafe deletions. Any delete-propagation logic MUST have the same safety gates as workspace-sync's: delete-sanity threshold (max N or max %, abort if exceeded), working-tree-size check, abort sentinel on suspicious deletion volume.

PROP-051 lineage: keep dome-mirror as a FULL clone (not sparse). The sparse-checkout exclusions for the 4 agents at PROP-084 do NOT apply to dome-mirror — see CLAUDE.md '~342 MB monitor/integrity bulk' note.
Do NOT modify prune-integrity.js itself — the git side is working correctly. Fix is in dome-mirror / sync-workspace-step4c.js.

Cleanup of existing FUSE orphans is being handled operator-side concurrent with this directive (via mcp__cowork__allow_cowork_file_delete). This directive is about preventing future accumulation, not draining the current backlog.
investigation_questions: Q1: What's the right deletion mechanism? Options: (a) walk monitor/integrity/ on FUSE, find files whose corresponding path no longer exists in the freshly-cloned git working tree, delete from FUSE — straightforward but needs safety gates; (b) parse git log since last sync sentinel for `D` mode entries, delete those specific paths — more surgical, lower blast radius; (c) just call git's working-tree sync mechanism (e.g., a checked-out copy operation) — simplest but may have other side effects.

Q2: What's the right safety gate threshold for delete-sanity? workspace-sync uses 50 deletions OR 10% of tree. dome-mirror has a different ratio because monitor/integrity/ has ~2-3K files normally so 100 deletions or 5% might be more appropriate.

Q3: Should the deletion propagation be opt-in by path prefix (only delete inside monitor/integrity/)? Pro: limits blast radius. Con: requires updating prefix list when new prune-eligible categories are added.
Q4: How does this interact with PROP-082's filter on the FUSE→git side? Does PROP-082 also need an update so the universal-pusher doesn't try to re-push files we just deleted from FUSE in this cycle?
deliverable: A PROP-NNN proposal in monitor/tinker/proposals/ with: (1) chosen deletion mechanism + rationale, (2) safety-gate thresholds, (3) interaction analysis with PROP-082, (4) test plan showing the delete-propagation correctly handles a single-file deletion case + does NOT fire on a 'origin recovered from a force-push reset' edge case (need to distinguish 'origin deleted file' from 'origin reverted to a state without the file but the file still belongs there'), (5) rollout plan with safety pauses if needed. Propose-only; operator integrates after review.
